What to verify: Check important pages and assets are not unintentionally disallowed.
Confirm canonical, indexable URLs are included and the sitemap is accessible.
Look for unintended meta robots or X-Robots-Tag noindex directives.
Investigate unexpected errors and redirect chains on important URLs.
Investigate exclusions and indexing issues using available search engine tools.
Redirect alternate HTTP/HTTPS and www/non-www versions consistently.
Ensure canonical URLs point to the intended preferred pages.
Fix links leading to missing pages or incorrect destinations.
Resolve loops and unnecessary redirect hops.
Write unique, descriptive titles for important pages.
Write useful summaries for key pages; search engines may choose other snippets.
Use descriptive headings in a logical order.
Describe meaningful images accurately and use empty alt for decorative images.
Use stable, descriptive URLs where practical.
Ensure content addresses the audience's likely needs and questions.
Verify facts, dates, examples, prices, and references.
Decide whether pages need improvement, consolidation, redirection, or no change.
Use original examples, clear authorship, and trustworthy references where relevant.
Link to important pages from relevant content.
Use concise, descriptive anchors that match the destination.
Identify important pages with no meaningful internal links.
Check navigation, forms, text, buttons, and horizontal overflow.

Check: Review Core Web Vitals and speed
What to verify: Use field data where available and lab diagnostics for opportunities.
Resize images and reduce unnecessary scripts, fonts, and CSS.
Verify secure loading and check key pages for broken layouts.
Test supported schema types and correct syntax errors.
Do not mark up information users cannot find on the page.
Confirm important leads or actions are measured appropriately.
Monitor clicks, impressions, queries, and important landing pages.
Record evidence, impact, owner, and next action for each issue.
